text:
elaine-marketing: Morning team  we need a final sanity check for the launch performance table. Request: run a shard-level validation on s3://redwood-prod/benchmarks/launch/2026-03/ with a reproducible 750-sample subset. Deliverables: raw CSVs, a single-slide PNG summary, and a one-paragraph methods blurb. Metrics: median + p95 for generation (per-token) and embeddings, plus quantized speedups (4-bit and 8-bit) vs float, and a small token-delta analysis. Please include cached vs cold comparisons and list the exact machines/runtime used. Target for internal publish; need outputs by EOD PST if feasible.

matt-eng-runtime: Got it. We'll run sample shard validation. A couple quick clarifications: (1) do you want seq_len distribution preserved or a controlled seq=512 run as well? (2) do you want prefix KV caching only or both prefix+session cache?

elaine-marketing: Preserve observed seq_len distribution, and yes also include a controlled seq=512 run for the headline table. For cache, show prefix-only cached vs cold (that's the primary story).

vikram-eng-runtime: I'll take this. Plan: deterministic selection from first shard, 750 samples, two sweep types: observed-dist and seq512. For each sweep: float32, 8-bit quant, 4-bit quant (where supported). Cache modes: cold and prefix_cached. I'll also add a parquet-schema validator step to detect any schema drift and report dropped rows. Repro command below:

```
# shard sanity run
tools/bench/run_shard_validate.sh \
  --s3 s3://redwood-prod/benchmarks/launch/2026-03/ \
  --samples 750 \
  --model redwood-large-v1 \
  --seq-dist observed \
  --controlled-seq 512 \
  --quantized float,8bit,4bit \
  --cache-modes cold,prefix_cached \
  --truncate 8192 \
  --output gs://bench-results/launch/1954409999/
```

bench-bot: Job queued: id=jb-20260324-9901, queue_pos=5, est_start=14m.

matt-eng-runtime: Note: some shards historically used nesting in the \"context\" field which breaks the current parser. We'll detect and drop those rows and include dropped_rows counts + examples. Also we'll limit long contexts to avoid OOMs per usual.

[~2h later]

vikram-eng-runtime: First sweep done. Uploaded CSVs to gs://bench-results/launch/1954409999/{shard-750-observed.csv, shard-750-512.csv, methods.md}. Key numbers (observed-dist, float): gen median=48ms/token, gen p95=145ms/token; embed median=14ms, embed p95=30ms. 8-bit quant speedup median ~1.6x, 4-bit ~2.7x (on gen). Token-delta (heldout-200) = 0.7% for 8-bit, 1.4% for 4-bit. Truncated_rows=5/750, dropped_schema_rows=2/750.

matt-eng-runtime: Cold vs cached: cold gen p95=270ms/token, prefix_cached p95=145ms/token. Controlled seq=512 run: gen median=60ms, p95=180ms. I also ran a small cold-only seq=1024 (100 samples) to show worst-case tail: cold seq1024 p95=410ms/token.

elaine-marketing: This is exactly the granularity we need. Two requests: (1) can you produce a compact slide-ready table with columns: sample_count, median_gen, p95_gen, median_embed, p95_embed, 8bit_speedup, 4bit_speedup, token_delta_8bit, token_delta_4bit, truncated_pct, dropped_pct, cached_vs_cold_p95_ratio? (2) please add a top-5 examples CSV where quantization changed tokenization or meaning so comms/legal can review.

vikram-eng-runtime: Will produce the slide table and top5-quant-affected.csv. I'll also include a methods.md with exact runtime tag: redwood-runtime v2.2.0, CUDA 12.2, cuDNN 9.x, and machine types used (A40 pool, one A100-80GB for quant checks). ETA ~25m.

zoe-legal: quick note: we're OK publishing these internal benchmarks as long as the methods blurb includes sample size, hardware, and the \"not a claim of product equivalence\" caveat. Please add that sentence to methods.md.

bench-bot: Job completed: id=jb-20260324-9901, duration=02:12:34.

vikram-eng-runtime: All artifacts uploaded: gs://bench-results/launch/1954409999/{shard-750-observed.csv, shard-750-512.csv, shard-100-cold1024.csv, slide-table.csv, top5-quant-affected.csv, methods.md, slide-summary.png}. Marking thread resolved unless marketing wants further sweeps.

elaine-marketing: Perfect  we'll pull the slide and method blurb and loop legal. Thanks everyone :rocket:
